name: Pediatric classic Hodgkin lymphoma: response-adapted ABVE-PC (AHOD0031); OEPA-COPDAC alternative

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

biomarkers.note: Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Pediatric Hodgkin Lymphoma v1.2026. Pediatric classic Hodgkin lymphoma therapy is response-adapted (interim FDG-PET Deauville response after 2 cycles), not biomarker-gated; no per-drug dose here is gated by a molecular biomarker (ped_hodgkin.txt lines 244, 650 to 656).

treatmentSetting: primary systemic therapy, response-adapted (interim FDG-PET after 2 cycles drives cycle number and involved-site radiotherapy)
supportiveCare: bleomycin PULMONARY toxicity: PFTs before use (FEV1/FVC >60% generally acceptable), monitor for pneumonitis, hold for pulmonary toxicity (ped_hodgkin.txt lines 397 to 399, 471)
anthracycline cardioprotection: strongly consider dexrazoxane for children/adolescents expected to receive >=250 mg/m2 cumulative doxorubicin-equivalent (ped_hodgkin.txt lines 320 to 322)
response-adapted: interim FDG-PET Deauville after 2 cycles determines cycle number and involved-site radiotherapy (ped_hodgkin.txt lines 244, 650 to 656)

alternative regimen OEPA-COPDAC (GPOH-HD-2002 / EuroNet-PHL-C1): OEPA = Vincristine 1.5 mg/m2 Days 1/8/15 (2 mg/dose max), Etoposide 125 mg/m2 Days 1 to 5, Prednisone 60 mg/m2 Days 1 to 15, Doxorubicin 40 mg/m2 Days 1 and 15, every 28 days x2; COPDAC = Cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m2 Days 1 and 8, Vincristine 1.5 mg/m2 Days 1 and 8 (2 mg/dose max), Prednisone 40 mg/m2 Days 1 to 15 (80 mg/day max), Dacarbazine 250 mg/m2 Days 1 to 3, every 28 days x2 or x4 by stage (ped_hodgkin.txt lines 1901 to 1928)
antiemetic and growth-factor support per NCCN tiers
monitoring: CBC with differential before each cycle
pulmonary function tests before bleomycin and if pulmonary symptoms develop
cardiac assessment and cumulative doxorubicin-equivalent tracking
interim and end-of-therapy FDG-PET/CT (Deauville) for response adaptation
peripheral neuropathy assessment before each vincristine dose

doseModificationRules.text: Hold bleomycin for pulmonary toxicity; physician decides on discontinuation.

doseModificationRules.condition: ANC < 1000 or platelets < 100k at cycle start
doseModificationRules.text: Review required. AHOD0031 count-recovery criteria apply; physician decides.

drugs.name: DOXOrubicin
drugs.notes: ABVE-PC 'A'. Printed dose 25 mg/m2 IV Days 1 and 2 (ped_hodgkin.txt line 1853). ISMP tall-man DOXOrubicin. Strongly consider dexrazoxane for children/adolescents expected to receive >=250 mg/m2 cumulative doxorubicin-equivalent (line 322), carried as the warn threshold; 350 mg/m2 is the conservative pediatric hard ceiling (below the adult 550; dexrazoxane per COG), matching the pediatric guard used in ped-neuroblastoma.

provenance.locator: ped_hodgkin.txt line 1853 (ABVE-PC AHOD0031: Doxorubicin 25 mg/m2 IV Days 1 and 2); dexrazoxane/cumulative-doxorubicin guidance lines 320 to 322

drugs.name: Bleomycin (Day 1)
drugs.notes: ABVE-PC 'B', Day 1 dose. Printed as 5 U/m2 IV on Day 1 (ped_hodgkin.txt line 1854); the Day 8 dose escalates to 10 U/m2 and is encoded as a separate Bleomycin (Day 8) entry so both days compute correctly. PULMONARY toxicity risk: obtain PFTs before use (FEV1/FVC >60% generally acceptable, line 471); monitor for pneumonitis and hold for pulmonary toxicity.

drugs.name: Bleomycin (Day 8)

PULMONARY toxicity risk: obtain PFTs before use (FEV1/FVC >60% generally acceptable, line 471); monitor for pneumonitis and hold for pulmonary toxicity.

drugs.name: vinCRIStine
drugs.notes: ABVE-PC 'V'. Printed dose 1.4 mg/m2 IV Days 1 and 8 (ped_hodgkin.txt line 1855). The source prints a 2.8 mg/dose pediatric maximum, but StewardMD carries the ISMP 2 mg per-dose cap as the safety default (see evidence.divergence). ISMP tall-man vinCRIStine; IV only and fatal if given intrathecally.
